correctness.rationale: For each fixed source word, constrained rank is one plus a collision count under a random linear map. Rank-d tuple counting gives all integer moments, Jensen/Lyapunov handle rho at least one, and a second-moment plus Paley-Zygmund argument handles fractional rho. Arikan's one-shot inequality then gives the all-rate exponent, while a cellwise converse proves optimality among all encoders. Small finite enumerations reproduce the exact first-moment formulas and the binary second-moment identity.

originality.rationale: The closest recent coset-guesswork theorem is stated only under subcriticality assumptions and does not cover the low-rate positive-part transition. Classical task-encoding work supplies arbitrary-encoder bounds and random-binning achievability, which are treated as prior art. Targeted searches found no prior statement that uniform random linear syndrome maps obey the source-independent constant-factor moment law or attain the resulting all-rate optimum. Residual folklore and adjacent-literature risk remains material.

value.rationale: The theorem closes the all-rate gap in a recent random-linear-code guesswork result, removes IID and weight-spectrum assumptions, proves structured linear maps exponent-optimal against arbitrary encoders, and identifies a moment-dependent phase transition with a heavy-tail moment cascade.
